title: CTDM: Resource-Efficient FPGA-Accelerated Simulation of Large-Scale NPU Designs
problem: Large-scale NPU simulations on FPGA face significant resource utilization challenges, limiting the ability to simulate large processor variants and enabling multi-FPGA deployments for comprehensive hardware verification.
motivation: Efficient FPGA-accelerated simulation is critical for NPU design verification and validation, enabling faster iteration cycles during hardware development without resorting to expensive full-system simulations.
method: CTDM introduces Chain-based Time-Division Multiplexing that replaces repeated logic patterns with single logic and register chains exploiting built-in shift register primitives. An automated CTDM compiler supports Verilog, VHDL, HLS, and Chisel across various FPGA devices. For multi-FPGA systems, block interleaving hides inter-FPGA link latency and fully utilizes high-speed serial I/O pipelines.
key_novelty: Chain-based Time-Division Multiplexing with automated compiler supporting multiple HDLs and enabling multi-FPGA deployments for large-scale NPU simulation with dramatically reduced resource overhead.
contributions: Chain-based TDM approach reducing FPGA resource overhead more effectively than multiplexer-based TDM
Automated CTDM compiler supporting Verilog, VHDL, HLS, and Chisel HDLs with wide FPGA device support
Block interleaving technique for multi-FPGA systems enabling high-speed I/O utilization
66% LUT and 82% FF reduction enabling largest NVDLA variant deployment on single FPGA; 3,653× simulation acceleration vs CPU

metrics.speedup: 3,653× vs Synopsys VCS on CPU; enables 4-die 1024 TFLOPS chiplet simulation on 144 FPGAs
metrics.other: successful deployment of largest NVDLA on single AMD U250 FPGA

limitations: Evaluation limited to NVIDIA NVDLA and proprietary NPUs; generalization to other NPU architectures and applicability to heterogeneous accelerator designs is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: FPGA-accelerated NPU simulation via chain-based TDM
